proposal.title: CAP / London 2 — Letwin role and AIONix relocation
proposal.reason: Align Letwin’s actor and recruitment event and the AIONix relocation event, process and agreement with the London home base and revised appointment agreement in package 1. Preserve the existing recruitment and relocation dates, separate California team leadership and the distinction between service vesting and issued shares.

before.name: Gordon Letwin
before.description: Copenhagen-based AION Software systems-software director and technical liaison to DRI, with a service-based equity grant. He remains in Denmark when the AIONix team relocates to California.

after.name: Gordon Letwin
after.description: London-based AION Software systems-software director and technical liaison to DRI, with a service-based equity grant. He remains in London when the AIONix team relocates to California.

before.title: Letwin recruited to Copenhagen systems-software leadership
before.description: Letwin eagerly accepts a move to Europe and joins AION Software in Copenhagen as Director of Systems Software and DRI Technical Liaison. He values the opportunity to build a team and collaborate with Kildall. AION supports relocation and US technical visits.

outcomes.description: Letwin never joins Microsoft in this scenario.
Letwin takes the Copenhagen-based systems-software role and receives a contractual four-year equity grant; this event does not establish completed vesting.

after.title: Letwin recruited to London systems-software leadership
after.description: Letwin eagerly accepts a move to London and joins AION Software as Director of Systems Software and DRI Technical Liaison, reporting to CEO Alex d’Agapeyeff. The English-speaking base and established CAP team support his European move. AION assists with relocation, required work permission, housing, Cambridge engineering visits and scheduled US technical visits.

outcomes.description: Letwin never joins Microsoft in this scenario.
Letwin takes the London-based systems-software role and receives a contractual four-year equity grant; this event does not establish completed vesting.

before.title: AIONix department relocates near DRI
before.description: On 24 February 1978, the AIONix department moves from Copenhagen to Logix offices near DRI headquarters. Letwin remains in Copenhagen to lead the systems-software group and liaise with DRI through scheduled visits. Separate day-to-day leadership is provided for the relocated AIONix team.

inputs.description: The AIONix exploratory architecture and portability work begun on 1 February provides the programme context for relocating its department closer to DRI.

outcomes.description: The AIONix department is based at Logix offices near DRI headquarters to support the continuing development programme. Letwin’s Copenhagen post is retained.

before.title: AIONix development programme and ownership formalised

party.role: Sponsor and transferor of the promised Logix equity
Computer-platform partner and host of the relocated AIONix team
AIONix owner, roadmap authority and development funder
Operating-system engineering partner and recipient of reuse and porting rights
Engineering partner and recipient of the promised Logix interest

before.description: Agreement identity reconstructed from the event and terms. Signing/other milestones remain separate events.

clauses.statement: DRI dedicates staff and operating-system expertise alongside AION Software.
AION Software covers DRI costs and expenses.
AION Software owns and controls the AIONix roadmap.

Adam promised Gary Kildall an 10% interest in Logix under the AIONix agreement of 12 September 1978. Adam fulfilled that promise in a single transfer on 12 October 1978 as part of the four-person share allocation.
DRI obtains rights to port AIONix to non-ERA processors in 1982.
DRI may reuse key AIONix components, but not Logix computer architecture or bus/I/O standards.

AIONix department moves from Copenhagen to Logix offices near DRI headquarters. Letwin remains in Copenhagen leading systems software and coordinating with DRI through scheduled visits; the relocated team has separate day-to-day leadership.

This separate AIONix agreement does not transfer CP/M ownership or restrict DRI’s independent CP/M OEM business. Existing AION ownership, Gary’s 10% Logix grant and the 1982 AIONix non-ERA porting right remain; replacing those specific terms requires a separate decision.

before.title: AIONix exploratory and formal development
before.description: Develop AIONix from the exploratory architecture and portability milestone on 1 February 1978 through completion of this development phase on 20 February 1980, under the separately agreed ownership and later non-ERA porting rights. Commercial release with Artemis follows on 19 May 1980.

outcomes.description: The AIONix development phase is complete for handover to later Artemis integration and launch preparation; this outcome does not move commercial availability before 19 May 1980.

steps.description: AION Software and DRI began architecture, C portability and ERA operating-system work in February 1978.
Move the AIONix department from Copenhagen to Logix offices near DRI headquarters on 24 February 1978. Letwin remains in Copenhagen; a separate lead manages the relocated team.
Milestone during this process: AIONix development programme and ownership formalised.
Following the September agreement, the teams developed the ERA operating system while maintaining CP/M and the Aurelia release line.
Complete the October Logix transfer: Kildall and Comstock receive 10% each, and the CFO and Paterson 5% each. The promised interests are fulfilled once.
Prepare confidential next-generation system software, application migration and C tools for Artemis without public disclosure before NCC 1980.
Complete this phase of AIONix development by 20 February 1980 and hand the work over for subsequent platform integration and commercial launch preparation. Ongoing maintenance continues separately.
